question: An announced investment at a summit should be treated as:

options.A: A policy or investor intention pending verification of actual deployment
options.B: Proof that all proposed jobs exist

source.observation: Government-linked India Investment Grid distinguishes project stage from actual financial and physical progress; lists completion certificate/COD and cautions project authority information needs investor due diligence.
Project listing separately identifies Idea Stage and total estimated project cost, showing proposal-stage costs are not automatically realised spending.

option_assessments.A: SUPPORTED_AS_BEST_ANSWER: an announcement is evidence of intention, not completion; actual deployment requires subsequent records.
option_assessments.B: INCORRECT: projected jobs are not employment realised.
option_assessments.C: INCORRECT: proposed investment and actual FDI inflows are different measures; no assertion that the proposal is foreign investment.
option_assessments.D: INCORRECT: investor announcements do not themselves enact a government appropriation.

limitations: Sources support stage/progress distinction, not a quantified summit-specific conversion rate.
No Telangana summit-specific announcement, MoU, expenditure, FDI transaction or employment register examined.
No independent expert signoff; no official PYQ claim.
